relevance_note: A literature review whose supplementary Table S1 lists 89 individual patients with per-patient TNFAIP3 alteration, sex, age of onset and features ('Table S1. Clinical characteristics of patients with HA20.').
method_note: Review of published HA20 cases; all 89 individuals come from supplementary Table S1 (converted from a PDF as fixed-width text, not a Markdown table). A Python script in my scratch directory parsed each patient row (Patient number, AOS, Gender and the ten +/- columns RF, Oral ulcers, Genital ulcers, Ocular, Skin lesion, Vasculitis, GI ulcers, MSD, AITD, RRTI) by token order; I checked its output against the table (89 rows, patients 1-89 in order; column totals for RF, ocular, vasculitis, GI, MSD, AITD, RRTI and sex match Table 1). The wrapped cells (Other manifestations, Treatment) were transcribed by hand from my reading and quoted line by line, because the PDF conversion interleaves the wrapped columns; non-contiguous lines are given as separate spans. Labels follow the bare-number Patient column: 'Table S1 #<n>'. The Family and Amino acid alteration cells are printed only on the first row of each family; later rows of the same family (blank cells, including rows after a '(Continued)' page header) were assigned to the family above them, and their family, variant and source-reference spans quote that first row. The per-patient reference is the number in brackets in the Family (Ref.) cell, which points to the References list under Table S1 (not the main reference list); source_reference_in_review gives the bracket and the matching Table S1 reference entry. Table symbols: '+' was read as present; '-' and '/' are not defined anywhere in the paper, so they were recorded as not reported (no excluded rows at all). AOS is in years ('AOS (y)'); ISO durations keep the decimal years (e.g. P0.75Y). AOS is blank for patients 36, 48, 70, 71, 72, 75, 86 and 89. The Initial diagnosis column was not converted into features or diagnoses (initial diagnoses such as BD were later revised to HA20); disease_label is HA20 from the Table S1 title. Checklist mapping was kept narrow: Ocular (text: 'ocular involvement'), MSD (musculoskeletal disorder) and AITD (autoimmune thyroid disorder) were NOT mapped to 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation', 'arthritis or arthralgia' or 'autoimmune thyroiditis', because the broader terms do not establish the narrower items; idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura and 'cytopenia' were not mapped to 'cytopenia (autoimmune)', plain 'hepatitis' not to autoimmune hepatitis, and pericardial effusion/ascites not to serositis. Atrophic gastritis was mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation', insulin-dependent diabetes to type 1 diabetes, growth delay to growth failure, aseptic meningitis and CNS vasculitis to CNS involvement, RRTI, recurrent urinary tract infections and repeated genital HSV infections to recurrent infections. Variant fields: zygosity heterozygous and gene TNFAIP3 come from the statement covering all 89 included patients; variant type, inheritance, pathogenicity and functional evidence are not given per patient (the paper's group counts list several classes), so not reported, except the exon 2-3 deletion, which the text names specifically. Only protein descriptions are printed, verbatim with the paper's spacing (e.g. 'p. Cys243Tyr', 'p. Arg 87*', 'p. Asn98Thrfs25' without an asterisk). Patient 43's treatment cell runs over nine lines; only five lines could be quoted, so the value marks the omitted middle with [...]. Contradictions in the paper: Table S1 gives 67 patients with oral ulcers, 37 with genital ulcers and 35 with skin lesions, whereas Table 1 and the text give 62 (70%), 32 (36%) and 34 (38%); Table S1 family numbers skip 31 and 32 (39 families listed, matching the text). Table S2 (counts per mutation) and Table 1-3 group counts were not used for individuals.
